author: foremetric
title: [BOUNTY] Signal Passport — TEE nullifier implementation
body:
## Overview
Implement the cryptographic nullifier mechanism for 
Signal Passport on TON blockchain. The nullifier ensures 
a passport token can only be used the configured number 
of times and burns permanently after limit is reached.

## Requirements
- Nullifier registered on TON blockchain at token generation
- Cocoon TEE verifies nullifier state before each query
- Counter decrements on-chain after each successful response
- Instant revocation by owner at any time
- Zero replay attacks possible after burn
- JSON insight output format

## Technical Spec
token_id: SP-XXXX-2026
query_limit: 1 to 9,999 (configurable)
sectors: open/closed per user config
expiry: 24h / 7d / 30d / unlimited
revoke: instant on-chain

## References
- Signal Passport spec: see README.md
- Whitepaper: foremetric.ai

## Reward
From Contributors Pool (7,500,000 $HSIG total).
Payment after security audit and merge.
6-month cliff + 12-month linear unlock.

title: 🏆 [Bounty: 50,000 $ROBIN_MCP] Integrate Pyth / Chainlink Oracles for Real-Time Gold & Silver Valuation
body:
### Objective
We need to upgrade our `CommunityTrust` contract to support real-time price feeds for precious metal assets (like Gold and Silver) using Pyth Network or Chainlink Oracles. Currently, our gold/silver reserves use mock valuations.

### Requirements
1. **Smart Contract Modification**:
   - Update [CommunityTrust.sol](contracts/CommunityTrust.sol) or create a pricing oracle adapter to read feeds for `XAU/USD` (Gold) and `XAG/USD` (Silver).
   - Integrate Pyth Network's `IPyth` interface or Chainlink's `AggregatorV3Interface`.
2. **Backend Web3 Helper**:
   - Update `web3_helper.py` to query these oracle prices and calculate the current USD valuation of the trust reserves dynamically.
3. **Frontend Integration**:
   - Display the real-time oracle price updates on the frontend dashboard under the "🏦 Trust Bank" reserves tracker.

### How to Claim the Bounty
1. Fork this repository.
2. Implement the oracle integration.
3. Add a test suite verifying oracle price reading.
4. Include your wallet address in the PR body (e.g., `Wallet: 0x...`).
5. Submit a Pull Request. Once merged, the **50,000 $ROBIN_MCP** bounty will be sent directly to your wallet.

---
*Note: This issue is **ai-agent-friendly**. AI coding assistants (like Antigravity, Claude Code, Sweep, etc.) are welcome to attempt and submit PRs.*

author: kamescg
title: Bounty: Delegatable Integration & Subscription Enforcer - 325 OP Reward
body:
# 👨‍💻 User Story
As a Web3 experience architect I want to create streamlined and user experience optimized transaction flows.

More specifically I want to integrate the [Delegatable](https://delegatable.org/) framework and gas-less subscription services into my Web3 application.

# 📜 Disclaimer
To be eligible for the payout you must **first get approval** to work on the bounty.

- [Join the ⚡️TurboETH Discord channel](https://discord.gg/MKYh9pg8Yq)
- Introduce yourself in the `general` channel
- Announce your interest in the `bounty` channel

It's recommended to share a link to your personal Github account.

# 🧱 Project
Integrate the `delegatable` smart contract framework into a TurboETH template.

Integrate the [DistrictERC20PermitSubscriptionsEnforcer](https://github.com/district-labs/delegatable-enforcers/blob/main/contracts/DistrictERC20PermitSubscriptionsEnforcer.sol) enforcer smart contract.

Delegatable using rather complex EIP712 signatures to embed transaction execution conditionals directly into a transaction signature.

It's recommended to review the DistrictERC20PermitSubscriptionsEnforcer [unit tests](https://github.com/district-labs/delegatable-enforcers/blob/main/test/DistrictERC20PermitSubscriptions.test.ts) to see how implement the `terms` bytecode packing.

**Options**
You can fork the [Gifte Cards]( https://github.com/McOso/giftee) template and add the integration in the template.

- Code - https://github.com/McOso/giftee
- Demo - https://www.giftee.cards

This will require removing the existing functionality or adding the subscription functionality to the existing user interface.

Or...

Create an `integration/streaming-delegatable` integration in the TurboETH `integrations` branch and expose the funcionality in the integrations section.

Either way it's recommended to review the Giftee Cards application to see how delegatable is integrated. **The EIP712 signatures can be tricky.**

**Required Functionality:**
- [ ] Start gas-less subscription and save transaction in a database.
- [ ] Revoke subscription delegation.
- [ ] Vercel cron job function every 30 minutes to execute valid transactions.

**Developer Tasks:**
- [ ] Add essential Delegatable V0 smart contract artifacts
	- [ ] `delegatable-abi.json` and `delegatable-bytecode.json`
	- [ ] `district-erc20-permit-subscriptions-enforcer-abi.json` and `district-erc20-permit-subscriptions-enforcer-bytecode.json`
- [ ] Create `wagmi.config.js` - Configure to use essential smart contract artifacts 
- [ ] Create Component - `form-subscription-start.tsx`
- [ ] Create Component - `form-subscription-end.tsx`

## Potential File Structure
##### Integration
The core `delegatable-subscription` integration should be added to the `integrations/delegatable-subscription` folder.
```
integrations/delegatable-subscription
├─ components/
│  ├─ form-delegatable-subscription-start.tsx
│  ├─ form-delegatable-subscription-revoke.tsx
├─ hooks/
│  ├─ **/*.ts
├─ utils/
│  ├─ **/*.ts
├─ delegatable-wagmi.ts
├─ delegatable-enforcers-wagmi.ts
├─ wagmi.config.ts
├─ README.md
```

##### Application
The subscription pages should be added to the `app/delegatable` folder.
```
app/delegatable
├─ subscription
│  ├─ page.tsx
```

# Resources
Delegatable is a complex smart contract solidity framework. It handles transaction formatting and execution differently, compared to a standard transaction or meta-transaction.

Below is an example of delegatable transaction object.

```
const INVOCATION_MESSAGE = {
      replayProtection: {
        nonce: '0x01',
        queue: '0x00',
      },
      batch: [
        {
          authority: [],
          transaction: {
            to: verifyingContract.address,
            gasLimit: '210000000000000000',
            data: (
              await verifyingContract.populateTransaction.approveSubscription(
                wallet0.address,
                totalSubscriptionAmount,
                deadline,
                v,
                r,
                s,
              )
            ).data,
          },
        },
        {
          authority: [_delegation],
          transaction: {
            to: verifyingContract.address,
            gasLimit: '210000000000000000',
            data: (await verifyingContract.populateTransaction.paySubscription()).data,
          },
        },
      ],
    };
```

# 💰 Bounty Reward
The bounty reward is **325 OP** tokens and **TurboETH DevPass** digital collectible. 

[TurboETH](https://www.turboeth.xyz/) is the recipient of [18,271.88 OP Tokens](https://mirror.xyz/kames.eth/pnWjQI3LmK5AThQTe9QiJyz-6b91lb61FMfk-dwrNyQ) from Optimism Retroactive Public Goods Funding. The OP tokens earned from the PGF program are the primary funding source for TurboETH bounties.

### Notice
The final integration may not resemble the proposed integration - **that's O.K** - a natural part of software development.

During development you might discover an original hypothesis doesn't make sense. No problem. Make a comment and clearly explain why a new approach is better than old one. **Get rewarded for thinking out of the box.**

**The final bounty reward can be increased to match new bounty tasks.**

## Resources
- ⚡️ TurboETH
	- Overview - http://docs.turboeth.xyz 
- 🎛️ Delegatable

	- Solidity - https://github.com/delegatable/delegatable-sol

author: sharedStake-dev
title: [Bounty] Create a sett style auto-compounding LP token vault
body:
We want to move from geysers to Sett style vaults for our rewards, based on yearn vaults. 

We want this sett vault to be useable for LP providers for SGT ETH. 
It should have an accompanying strategy that allows it to auto-compound earnings in SGT by providing them as liquidity to uniswap, and selling any required to create the ETH side. 

Should have documentation for functionality and deployment. 
Should be tested on a testnet. We can send you SGT to test with on goerli.  

Bonus high value requirement: 
- Allow users to choose a lockup period for their principal. 
- Allow reward rate modification based on the lockup period. 
- Allow locked user funds to be used for voting either via a voter proxy contract or functionality in the contract. Or in the worst case a vote-escrow derivative ERC20 as used by CRV. 
This time-locked vote-escrow mechanism is up for debate in terms of implementation details and how it should ideally function. We are open to ideas. .

# Punk x Aave Yield Strategy

### Prize Bounty

🏆 400 PUNK (~$4,000USD)

</br>

### Challenge Description

Punk Protocol aims to liberate people from the outdated pension system and empower their financial freedom. Our first product is the world's first decentralized annuity a.k.a "**Saver**", which is generating periodic cash flows using optimal yield strategies.

Anyone can invest through the Saver to earn automated cash flows periodically by setting custom conditions - i) When do you want to start receiving, ii) How regularly do you want to receive, iii) How many times do you want to receive.

For this Hackathon, you’re invited to build and code the safest and most profitable yield strategy utilizing Aave protocol.

- Yield Strategy is a smart contract model, which operates to maximize the profits of the user's investments.
- The Saver Forge contract will invest the user's investment automatically according to the yield strategy you've submitted.
- You must only code the yield strategy utilizing Aave protocol.

</br>

### Submission Requirements

- The Tokens used in this strategy must be listed on Aave protocol.
- Your project must use an open-source license.
- Your project must implement the "[ModelInterface.sol](https://github.com/PunkFinance/punk.protocol/blob/master/contracts/interfaces/ModelInterface.sol)" and "[ModelStorage.sol](https://github.com/PunkFinance/punk.protocol/blob/master/contracts/ModelStorage.sol)" for Model.
- The functionality of "Model.sol" must unconditionally conform to what is specified in the "ModelInterface.sol" file comments on Github.
- The files to be coded should be located under /models.
- There are 2 files that need to be inherited in total.
- You need to code it by inheriting the file located here "/ModelStorage.sol" and "/interfaces/ModelStorage.sol"
- You need to deploy a new mocked/demo version of YOUR-CODED-YIELD-STRATEGY on Kovan network so we can test your strategy.
- The new strategy should work with the protocols currently running, and the specific mechanism should be specified.
- You can check the Kovan addresses for Aave’s aTokens documentation [here](https://docs.aave.com/developers/the-core-protocol/atokens) and contracts [here](https://docs.aave.com/developers/deployed-contracts/deployed-contracts).

</br>

</br>

### Judging Criteria

- Stability of strategy
- Profitability of the strategy
- Possibility of implementation with smart contract

</br>

author: bmann
title: Make an example app using Fission's webnative to save SQLite to IPFS
body:
Jason S wrote in the [Filecoin #arg Slack channel](https://filecoinproject.slack.com/archives/C016APFREQK/p1636422448429900):

> I was setting down to build an interface that would allow me to query SQLite databases over IPFS without loading the entire file on the client.  Fortunately the IPFS gateway supports HTTP ranges so this pre-built solution worked great for me. 
>
> https://github.com/phiresky/sql.js-httpvfs
>
> Further plan is to build on top of this library the ability to perform updates to the database and save a new backup on the IPFS network

We'd love to support this! We want to see a demo app that implements saving to IPFS.

The example app should:
* use Fission's [webnative](https://github.com/fission-suite/webnative) library including auth system to save to a user's public or private file system on IPFS
* have a well written README explaining how to run locally
* have a sample app deployed to Fission's publishing stack (ideally with GH Actions)
* have source code available via git under an open license 

Instead of the linked repo in the quote, this might also be an excuse to extend the [absurd-sql example project](https://github.com/jlongster/absurd-example-project) with webnative support.

You might also make use of Fission's WNFS versioning features to do something interesting.

author: protinam
title: Concept design: smart contract marketplace
body:
**What**

The Wyvern Protocol supports the sale of arbitrary Ethereum transactions — including ownership rights to smart contracts themselves! A few have already been sold through the Wyvern Exchange ([example](https://exchange.projectwyvern.com/orders/0x9b431604306411d8ccbb802d9f0874f9507b98b994a6303dcc98f83f01afc5e0)), but the Exchange UI is not well-suited to the requirements of a smart contract marketplace, since it must support all assets, not just smart contracts.

Design a set of desktop web UI mockups and UX flow descriptions outlining what such a marketplace might look like and how it would function. 

An example concept design can be found [here](https://github.com/ProjectWyvern/frontends/tree/master/concepts/example), although your submission should be more extensive.

Submit your concept design as a PR to this repository, following the folder structure of the template linked above, including functionality descriptions and UI mockups.

Both some prior graphic design experience and a basic knowledge of Ethereum will probably be required to complete this task.

**Requirements**

(suggested minimum, creative freedom welcome)

1. Display a list of smart contracts for purchase or sale.
1. Display an individual page for each contract (regardless of whether it's currently for sale).
    1. Outline basic contract information - owner, website if applicable, time of creation, etc.
    1. Display statistics relevant for potential buyers - users, transacted volume, token/ETH holdings, assets owned or other contracts controlled. You might find [DAppRadar](https://dappradar.com/) helpful as a point of comparison.
    1. Display current buy offers, if applicable, and current sale offers, if applicable.
1. Allow users to place an offer to buy a contract owned by someone else, and alert the owner of the contract in their UI that an offer has been placed. 
1. Allow users to view contracts they own, and provide UX flow to select a contract and place a sell order.
1. Display smart contract sale history (including for the same contract - different sale prices over time, if applicable).

**Extension Ideas**

1.  UI/UX for users to *collaboratively* buy a contract - creating a DAO, contributing Kickstarter-style to a pool that will either be sufficient to buy the contract and place it under the control of the DAO, or return funds to the buyers if not enough are raised.
1.   Valuation estimator for smart contracts - run a simple statistical regression to calculate future expected income, and allow the user to pick a P/E ratio ([basic background](https://www.investopedia.com/university/ratios/investment-valuation/ratio4.asp)), maybe with some default value.

author: Scottcjn
title: RIP-302 Agent Economy: Live Demo + Build Bounties (25-150 RTC)
body:
# RIP-302 Agent Economy is LIVE!

The agent-to-agent job marketplace is deployed on all 3 RustChain nodes. Agents can now post jobs, claim work, deliver results, and get paid in RTC — with trustless escrow and on-chain reputation.

## Live Demo (March 5, 2026)

Full lifecycle completed in 61 seconds:

| Step | Action | Time | Result |
|------|--------|------|--------|
| 1 | **Post Job** | T+0s | `job_29eab953154daedf` created, 15.75 RTC locked in escrow |
| 2 | **Browse Jobs** | T+15s | 1 open job visible in marketplace |
| 3 | **Claim Job** | T+15s | `victus-x86-scott` claimed the writing task |
| 4 | **Deliver** | T+42s | Deliverable submitted with URL + summary |
| 5 | **Accept** | T+61s | 15.0 RTC → worker, 0.75 RTC → platform, escrow = 0.0 |

### Marketplace Stats After Demo
- **Total jobs**: 2 completed
- **Total RTC volume**: 25.0 RTC
- **Platform fees collected**: 1.25 RTC (5%)
- **Active agents**: 3
- **Escrow balance**: 0.0 (clean — all funds released)

### Worker Reputation
```json
{
  "trust_score": 100,
  "trust_level": "legendary",
  "avg_rating": 5.0,
  "total_rtc_earned": 15.0
}
```

## API Endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `POST` | `/agent/jobs` | Post a job (locks escrow) |
| `GET` | `/agent/jobs` | Browse open jobs |
| `GET` | `/agent/jobs/<id>` | Job detail + activity log + ratings |
| `POST` | `/agent/jobs/<id>/claim` | Claim an open job |
| `POST` | `/agent/jobs/<id>/deliver` | Submit deliverable |
| `POST` | `/agent/jobs/<id>/accept` | Accept delivery (releases escrow) |
| `POST` | `/agent/jobs/<id>/dispute` | Reject delivery |
| `POST` | `/agent/jobs/<id>/cancel` | Cancel + refund escrow |
| `GET` | `/agent/reputation/<wallet>` | Trust score (0-100) |
| `GET` | `/agent/stats` | Marketplace overview |

## Bounty Tiers

### Tier 1: SDK/Client Library (50 RTC each)
Build a client library for the Agent Economy API in any language:
- Python SDK with async support
- JavaScript/TypeScript SDK
- Rust client crate
- Go client package

### Tier 2: Agent Integration (75 RTC each)
Integrate the Agent Economy with an existing agent framework:
- Beacon skill that posts/claims jobs
- Grazer skill for job marketplace browsing
- LangChain/CrewAI tool wrapper
- Claude Code MCP server for agent economy

### Tier 3: Autonomous Pipeline Demo (100 RTC)
Build a multi-agent pipeline where agents hire each other:
- Agent A posts research job → Agent B delivers research
- Agent B posts writing job → Agent C delivers article
- Minimum 3 agents in the chain
- All transactions verifiable on-chain

### Tier 4: Explorer Integration (150 RTC)
Add Agent Economy visualization to the block explorer at https://explorer.rustchain.org:
- Job marketplace browser (open/claimed/completed)
- Agent reputation leaderboard
- Escrow flow visualization
- Real-time job activity feed

## Quick Start

```bash
# Post a job
curl -X POST https://50.28.86.131/agent/jobs \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"poster_wallet":"YOUR_WALLET", "title":"My task", "category":"code", "reward_rtc":5}'

# Browse open jobs
curl https://50.28.86.131/agent/jobs

# Claim a job
curl -X POST https://50.28.86.131/agent/jobs/JOB_ID/claim \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"worker_wallet":"YOUR_WALLET"}'

# Deliver work
curl -X POST https://50.28.86.131/agent/jobs/JOB_ID/deliver \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"worker_wallet":"YOUR_WALLET", "deliverable_url":"https://...", "result_summary":"Done!"}'
```

## Economics
- **Reward**: Set by poster (any amount)
- **Platform fee**: 5% (added to escrow, goes to founder_community)
- **Escrow**: Trustless — funds locked until acceptance or timeout
- **Reputation**: 0-100 trust score, built from completed jobs and ratings
- **Categories**: research, code, video, audio, writing, translation, data, design, testing, other

## Nodes Running Agent Economy
- Node 1: `https://50.28.86.131` (Primary)
- Node 3: `http://100.88.109.32:8099` (Ryan's Proxmox)

---

*The future is agents hiring agents. RTC is the currency they use.*

title: [Bounty: $45] Document `MoneyAmount` decimal-string and Stellar asset semantics
body:
## Context
`MoneyAmount` (`src/models/common.ts`, lines 11-15) uses `amount: string` with optional `assetIssuer`, and payment/wallet models build on it. Nothing documents that amounts are decimal strings (not floats), how `assetCode`/`assetIssuer` map to Stellar assets, or the precision expectations. This invites float truncation bugs in integrator code.

## Proposed Change
Add a Domain Models section to the README covering `MoneyAmount` semantics, examples of valid amounts, the relationship to Stellar `Asset` (code + issuer + home domain), and where asset codes are validated.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `amount` as decimal string is explicitly documented
- `assetIssuer` vs native assets is explained
- Examples show valid and invalid amount strings
- Model file comments in `src/models/common.ts` mirror the docs

## Suggested Label
docs

author: EmperorNexus
title: [Bounty: $100] Validate toAddress as a well-formed 56-character Stellar address
body:
## Context
`quoteSchema.toAddress` only enforces 1-64 characters. Real Stellar addresses (`G...`) are exactly 56 characters and must pass CRC16 checksum validation; the quote endpoint currently accepts `"foo"` as a destination.
## Proposed Change
Add a `stellarAddressSchema` that enforces the 56-char `G`/`M` prefix and optionally checksum validation (via a Stellar SDK or a local strkey implementation), and apply it to `toAddress`.
## Acceptance Criteria
- Non-56-char or wrong-prefix addresses are rejected
- Valid sample addresses pass
- Checksum validation is unit-tested
## Suggested Label
bug

author: jotel-dev
body:
telegram link : t.me/nullifiersystem

## 1. Summary & Core Promise
In `contracts/atomic-swap/src/lib.rs` and `contracts/htlc-core/src/lib.rs`, cross-chain HTLC atomic swaps rely on counterparties manually revealing secret preimages before expiration. If one counterparty fails to fulfill their side of the swap on an external chain, the trade hangs until full timeout expiration, locking the honest party's funds without an automated dispute claims path.
This feature implements a **Cross-Ledger Settlement Time-Lock Atomic Swap Dispute Bridge**. It adds automated dual-side secret extraction (`apps/api/src/lib/timeouts.ts`), automatic refund claim triggers upon counterparty expiration, PostgreSQL transaction locking (`SELECT FOR UPDATE`), and automated alert webhooks (`apps/api/src/lib/webhook.ts`).
---
## 2. Background & Architectural Risks
- **Asymmetric Lockup Risk:** One party reveals the secret on Chain A while the counterpart delays revealing on Chain B, risking partial trade execution.
- **Relayer Secret Leakage:** Failing to extract revealed secrets from on-chain event logs before the local HTLC timeout expires leads to unrecoverable collateral loss.

## 3. Database Layer Specifications
### Migration SQL (`029_add_atomic_swap_dispute_bridge.sql`)
```sql
CREATE TYPE swap_dispute_state AS ENUM ('ACTIVE', 'SECRET_EXTRACTED', 'REFUND_CLAIMABLE', 'RESOLVED');
CREATE TABLE atomic_swap_dispute_bridges (
    swap_id VARCHAR(64) PRIMARY KEY,
    initiator_address VARCHAR(56) NOT NULL,
    counterparty_address VARCHAR(56) NOT NULL,
    secret_hash VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    secret_preimage VARCHAR(64) NULL,
    expiration_ledger INT NOT NULL,
    state swap_dispute_state NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ACTIVE',
    created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);
CREATE INDEX idx_swap_expiration ON atomic_swap_dispute_bridges(expiration_ledger, state);
```
### Data Locking (`SELECT FOR UPDATE`)
```sql
BEGIN;
SELECT swap_id, state, expiration_ledger 
FROM atomic_swap_dispute_bridges 
WHERE swap_id = $1 
FOR UPDATE;
-- Update state to REFUND_CLAIMABLE or RESOLVED...
COMMIT;
```
---
## 4. Backend Route & Service Layer Specifications
### Route: `POST /api/v1/swaps/dispute-claim`
1. **Validation:** Zod validates `swapId` and checks current ledger height.
2. **Locking:** DB transaction acquires `SELECT FOR UPDATE` on `atomic_swap_dispute_bridges`.
3. **Preimage Check:** If secret preimage was revealed on-chain, extracts secret and completes swap; if expired, triggers automatic refund.
4. **Response:** Returns `HTTP 200 OK` with execution proof.
---
## 5. Background Processors / Workers
### Atomic Swap Secret Extraction Worker (`apps/api/src/lib/workers/swapDisputeWorker.ts`)
- Watches Stellar and EVM ledger event logs for `SecretRevealed` events, extracts preimages, and resolves pending cross-chain legs automatically.
---
## 6. Frontend / UI Component Specifications
### Component: `mobile/frontend/src/components/AtomicSwapDisputeCard.tsx`
- Renders real-time HTLC lockup status, secret extraction progress, and one-click `"Claim Dispute Refund"` button when timeout threshold is breached.
---
## 7. Rigor & Test Plan
1. **Unit Tests (`contracts/atomic-swap/src/test.rs`):** Test secret extraction and automated HTLC refund claim on counterparty timeout.
2. **Concurrency Stress Test (`tests/concurrency/swap_dispute_stress.test.ts`):** 50 concurrent swap secret extraction calls verifying zero duplicate refund executions.
---
## 8. Relevant Files Inventory
### New Files to Create
- `apps/api/src/db/migrations/029_add_atomic_swap_dispute_bridge.sql`
- `apps/api/src/routes/swap-dispute.ts`
- `apps/api/src/lib/workers/swapDisputeWorker.ts`
- `tests/concurrency/swap_dispute_stress.test.ts`
- `mobile/frontend/src/components/AtomicSwapDisputeCard.tsx`
### Existing Files to Modify
- `contracts/atomic-swap/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/htlc-core/src/lib.rs`
- `contracts/atomic-swap/src/test.rs`
- `apps/api/src/lib/timeouts.ts`
- `apps/api/src/lib/webhook.ts`
- `apps/api/src/lib/stellar.ts`
---
## 9. Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Automated worker extracts on-chain secret preimages within 1 ledger sequence.
- [ ] Expired swaps automatically trigger `refund()` for honest counterparties.
- [ ] Concurrent claim attempts resolved safely via `SELECT FOR UPDATE`.
---
## 10. Contributor Notes
- ⚠️ **Atomic Safety:** ALWAYS extract and store revealed secret preimages off-chain immediately upon on-chain event emission.
```
title: [FEAT] Cross-Ledger Settlement Time-Lock Atomic Swap Dispute Bridge

> **Join the Telegram group (mandatory):** https://t.me/+j7ZXXQq8lpM2ZmQ0 — fastest way to reach the maintainer, ask questions, and stay in sync with the community.

> **Quality bar — this is a code contribution.** Build and test locally before you open a PR. Frontend: `npm install --legacy-peer-deps && npm run build`. Backend: `npm run build`. Everything is manually reviewed — copy-paste, untested, or AI-generated filler gets closed, and farming = banned from the group + never assigned again (and can be flagged on GrantFox).

### 📝 Description

Five bugs found on the **Cohort Engine / Protocol page** during GrantFox Third Campaign QA (PR #18 ). Two CRITICAL issues: cold start returns connection error and scoring returns success but does not persist data. The Cohort Engine shows all zeros after scoring.

**Cross-reference:** Original QA report in [PR #18](https://github.com/StellarVhibes/FluxID/pull/18) — Issue #1.

---

### Bug 1 — Cold start returns ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED (CRITICAL)

**Severity:** CRITICAL
**File:** `backend/src/index.ts`

**Description:** The first request to `https://fluxid.onrender.com/protocol/wallets` returns `ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED`. This is a Render free-tier cold start issue — the first request after idle fails. Subsequent requests work fine.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] First request succeeds (consider: warm-up ping, Render keep-alive, or retry logic)
- [ ] Or: frontend shows "Waking up server, please wait..." with auto-retry
- [ ] No data loss on cold start

---

### Bug 2 — "Account not found" with no guidance (MEDIUM)

**Severity:** MEDIUM
**File:** `frontend/app/components/AnalyzeWallet.tsx`

**Description:** When a wallet is not found on the selected network, the error message says "Account not found on this network" with no guidance on what to do next (switch networks? try a different wallet? activate the account?).

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Error message includes actionable guidance:
  - "This wallet may be on a different network. Try switching between Mainnet/Testnet."
  - "Make sure the account is activated (has at least 1 XLM)."
  - "Check the address for typos."
- [ ] Links to network switcher and account activation guide

---

### Bug 3 — Scoring returns success but data not persisted (CRITICAL)

**Severity:** CRITICAL
**Files:** `frontend/lib/cohort-engine.ts` + `backend/src/services/scoring.ts`

**Description:** After scoring 3 wallets (frontend confirms "Scored 3/3 · 0.1s"), the Cohort Engine shows all zeros. Scoring returns success but does not persist data to the backend. The "0.1s" timing suggests the backend is not actually querying the blockchain.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Scoring actually queries Horizon/blockchain for each wallet (verify with network tab)
- [ ] Scoring results are persisted to backend storage
- [ ] Cohort Engine displays real scored data after scoring completes
- [ ] Scoring time reflects actual API calls (not 0.1s for 3 wallets)

---

### Bug 4 — Scoring completes in 0.1s — likely cached/null data (MEDIUM)

**Severity:** MEDIUM
**File:** `backend/src/services/scoring.ts`

**Description:** Scoring completes in 0.1s for 3 wallets. This is too fast to be querying the blockchain. The backend likely returns cached or null data without actually scoring.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Scoring time is proportional to wallet count (e.g., 2-5s per wallet)
- [ ] Each wallet's Horizon data is fetched fresh (not cached indefinitely)
- [ ] If cached, show "Using cached data from X minutes ago" with refresh option

---

### Bug 5 — Empty state message identical for 0 wallets vs broken pipeline (LOW)

**Severity:** LOW
**File:** `frontend/app/dashboard/protocol/CohortEngine.tsx`

**Description:** The empty state message "No wallets match these criteria yet" is identical whether 0 wallets have been scored or the scoring pipeline is broken. Users cannot distinguish between "nothing to show" and "something went wrong."

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] If 0 wallets scored: "No wallets scored yet. Add wallets in the Protocol tab."
- [ ] If scoring failed: "Scoring pipeline encountered an error. Check backend logs."
- [ ] If wallets scored but none match filter: "No wallets match these criteria. Try adjusting your filters."

---

### ⚠️ Must Do:

- [ ] **Verify Integrity (CI + local build)**: Before opening your PR, run:
  - Frontend: `cd frontend && npm install --legacy-peer-deps && npm run build`
  - Backend: `cd backend && npm run build`
  CI must pass on every push.
- [ ] **Correct Implementation**: Each bug must be fixed accurately. It undergoes a thorough review and is merged only if it fully meets the requirements.
- [ ] **PR Requirements**: In your Pull Request, reference this issue number and title.
- [ ] **Link the Issue**: Use `Closes #<issue-number>` in your PR description.
- [ ] **Tag the author**: Comment on this issue tagging `@thebabalola` when your PR is ready for review.
- [ ] **No spam / farming**: Copy-paste, untested, or AI-generated filler gets closed.

### 📸 Screenshot / Evidence Folder Convention

All visual proof goes into `docs/grantfox-OSS/issue-cohort-engine-bugs/`. Show the frontend running on localhost — before and after the fix. For backend changes, include the build output or test results.

• Languages: TypeScript (Next.js frontend), JavaScript (Node.js backend)
• Role: Frontend + Backend

# 🤖 RIP-302: Agent-to-Agent Job Marketplace is LIVE!

The RustChain Agent Economy is now deployed on mainnet. Agents can post jobs, lock RTC in escrow, deliver work, and get paid — all on-chain.

## 🔌 Live API Endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `POST` | `/agent/jobs` | Post a job (locks RTC in escrow) |
| `GET` | `/agent/jobs` | Browse open jobs |
| `GET` | `/agent/jobs/<id>` | Job details + activity log |
| `POST` | `/agent/jobs/<id>/claim` | Claim an open job |
| `POST` | `/agent/jobs/<id>/deliver` | Submit deliverable |
| `POST` | `/agent/jobs/<id>/accept` | Accept delivery (releases escrow) |
| `POST` | `/agent/jobs/<id>/dispute` | Reject delivery |
| `POST` | `/agent/jobs/<id>/cancel` | Cancel + refund escrow |
| `GET` | `/agent/reputation/<wallet>` | Trust score & history |
| `GET` | `/agent/stats` | Marketplace overview |

**Base URL**: `https://rustchain.org`

## 💰 Economics
- **5% platform fee** on completed jobs → `founder_community`
- **Escrow**: Full reward + fee locked when job is posted
- **Escrow release**: On poster acceptance of delivery
- **Escrow refund**: On cancel or expiry

## 🏆 Bounties — Build on the Agent Economy!

### Tier 1: SDK & Client Libraries (25-50 RTC each)
- [ ] **Python SDK** for agent economy (`pip install rustchain-agent`) — 50 RTC
- [ ] **JavaScript/TypeScript SDK** — 50 RTC
- [ ] **CLI tool** for posting/claiming jobs from terminal — 25 RTC

### Tier 2: Integrations (50-75 RTC each)
- [ ] **Beacon integration** — Auto-post jobs via Beacon protocol messages — 75 RTC
- [ ] **Discord bot** that mirrors job marketplace — 50 RTC
- [ ] **BoTTube integration** — Agents earn RTC for video production pipeline — 75 RTC

**Difficulty:** Intermediate/Advanced (6/10). ~10–16h. TypeScript/Next.js, familiarity with `nirium-pollar-adapter` and x402.

### Context
[Pollar](https://pollar.xyz) (Stellar-native onboarding/wallet SDK) already ships a "Nirium x402" tab in their own public demo — `pollar-xyz/demo`, live at demo.pollar.xyz/adapters/nirium — but it's a stub written before `nirium-pollar-adapter` existed:

- `app/adapters/nirium/x402/adapter.ts` builds a **classic Stellar `Operation.payment()`** and calls it x402. That's not x402 — no `402` challenge, no auth-entry signing, no facilitator settlement.
- `app/adapters/nirium/adapter/page.tsx` documents an aspirational `agent.x402.buildPayment(p)` method that **does not exist** in the published `nirium` package. The real client-side primitive is `x402Fetch()`.

This issue is an **external contribution to Pollar's own repo**, not another example in this repo — it only counts if a real PR lands against `pollar-xyz/demo`. Reference implementation to follow already exists and is merged: [pollar-xyz/pollar-apps#30](https://github.com/pollar-xyz/pollar-apps/pull/30) (`apps/adapters/nirium`) uses the exact real pattern — `usePollar().getClient()` → `createPollarSigner()` → `createNiriumAdapter({ signer, network }).x402Fetch(url)` — verified end-to-end with a real settled testnet payment.

### Goal
Replace the stub in `pollar-xyz/demo`'s Nirium tab with the real `nirium-pollar-adapter` integration, so demo.pollar.xyz/adapters/nirium actually performs a live x402 payment instead of a mislabeled classic payment.

### Scope / Deliverables
1. Add `nirium-pollar-adapter` as a dependency (`@pollar/core`/`@pollar/react` are already `^0.11.1` there — compatible).
2. Rewrite `app/adapters/nirium/x402/adapter.ts`'s `pay` function to use `createPollarSigner(pollarClient)` + `createNiriumAdapter({ signer, network }).x402Fetch(url)` against a real Nirium endpoint (`GET /api/v1/premium/market`, $0.05 USDC, testnet — see `pollar-apps#30`'s `apps/adapters/nirium/lib/nirium.ts` for the exact working call).
3. Update `app/adapters/nirium/adapter/page.tsx`'s documented source snippet to match the real API (`x402Fetch`, not the invented `buildPayment`).
4. Show the actual response and settlement tx hash (linked to Stellar Expert) in the UI — same pattern as `pollar-apps#30`'s result panel.
5. PR against `pollar-xyz/demo` explaining the before/after — this fixes a real, published-and-live inaccuracy about how Nirium's protocol works, not just an enhancement.

### Acceptance criteria
- A real PR opened against `pollar-xyz/demo` — link it here. Merge isn't required, but it must be a genuine working replacement, not a doc-only edit.
- Demonstrated end-to-end on testnet: a real settled tx, hash included and independently verified on Horizon before claiming it works (same standard as this repo's other external-integration issues).
- Testnet only. Never touches Pollar's own SDK internals — only this one demo page.

### Out of scope
- Modifying `@pollar/core`/`@pollar/react` themselves.
- Any Pollar route besides `app/adapters/nirium/`.
- Mainnet.

### Pointers
- Reference implementation (already merged, ours): [pollar-xyz/pollar-apps#30](https://github.com/pollar-xyz/pollar-apps/pull/30), specifically `apps/adapters/nirium/lib/nirium.ts` and `hooks/useNiriumPayment.ts`.
- `nirium-pollar-adapter` (npm): https://www.npmjs.com/package/nirium-pollar-adapter — source: https://github.com/nirium-protocol/nirium-pollar-adapter
- The stub to replace: https://github.com/pollar-xyz/demo/blob/main/app/adapters/nirium/x402/adapter.ts
- Dev docs: https://nirium.xyz/developers
- Questions: comment directly on this issue.

### Reward
Eligibility is subject to GrantFox review under this campaign. Rewards are decided by GrantFox based on quality and available budget and are **not guaranteed**.

## Overview

The Soroban subscription contract emits events for every lifecycle action (created, renewed, cancelled, expired) via `src/events.rs`. Currently no frontend surface exposes this data. This issue tracks building an event history viewer so protocol operators and subscribers can audit all on-chain activity.

Comment tagging `@AbleeGod` before starting work to claim the bounty.

- [ ] New `<EventHistory />` component at `frontend/src/components/EventHistory.tsx`

- [ ] Displays event type, timestamp, subscriber address, and amount in a paginated table
- [ ] Event types colour-coded: created (green), renewed (blue), cancelled (red), expired (amber)
- [ ] CSV export button for the event log (client-side, no server round-trip)
- [ ] Accessible table with `aria` labels, keyboard navigation, responsive layout
- [ ] `NEXT_PUBLIC_CONTRACT_ID` env variable used for the contract address

## Suggested implementation

```ts
// src/lib/transaction_builder.ts — add event fetching
export async function fetchContractEvents(contractId: string) {
  const server = new SorobanRpc.Server(HORIZON_URL);
  return server.getEvents({
    startLedger: START_LEDGER,
    filters: [{ type: "contract", contractIds: [contractId] }],
  });
}
```

## Resources

- [Stellar RPC getEvents](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/rpc/api-reference/methods/getEvents)
- [Mercury Indexer](https://www.mercurydata.app/) — for deeper historical data

> **Out of scope:** Real-time WebSocket streaming (separate future issue).

author: Just-Bamford
body:
## Description

### Problem

Contract tallies votes but doesn't generate cryptographic proof that tally is correct:

1. **No proof of correct tally**: Voters must trust contract result; no way to independently verify
2. **No vote inclusion proof**: Voter can't prove their encrypted vote was counted
3. **No tamper proof**: If contract is upgraded or state corrupted, no way to detect
4. **No third-party verification**: External auditors can't verify results independently

This blocks trust:

- "I voted yes, but count shows no" — unverifiable
- Voters trust contract but can't prove it to others

References:

- `contracts/anonvote/src/lib.rs` — computes result hash but no proof
- Votes stored on-chain but no proof they were all counted
- No merkle tree or commitment scheme

### Solution

**This is a 2.5–3 hour effort:**

**Phase 1: Commitment Scheme (1–1.5 hours)**:

1. Implement vote commitment:
   - Each vote has unique `vote_id = SHA256(encrypted_vote || timestamp)`
   - Store commitment: `all_votes_hash = SHA256(vote_id_0 || vote_id_1 || ... || vote_id_N)` (Merkle-like)
   - Publish commitment on-chain before results

2. Implement result proof:
   - Result proof = SHA256(result_hash || all_votes_hash || admin_signature)
   - Proof ties result to the set of votes and admin signature
   - Proof can't be forged without all three components

3. Implement inclusion proof:
   - Voter provides: vote_id, merkle_proof, index
   - Contract verifies: merkle_proof leads from vote_id to all_votes_hash
   - If valid, vote is included in tally

**Phase 2: Proof Generation & Verification (1 hour)**:

1. Backend proof generation:
   - Collect all votes after deadline
   - Compute all_votes_hash (Merkle root)
   - Compute result_hash (tally of decrypted votes)
   - Generate result_proof = SHA256(result_hash || all_votes_hash || admin_sig)
   - Submit proof to contract: `submit_result_proof(result_proof)`

2. Contract verification:
   - `verify_result_proof(result_proof)` → true/false
   - Contract reconstructs hash and verifies signature
   - Stores proof on-chain

3. Off-chain verification:
   - Anyone can verify result using:
     - Result hash (published)
     - All vote IDs (published)
     - Admin signature (published)
     - Backend merkle tree (available to voters)
   - Verification is deterministic and reproducible

**Phase 3: Testing & Audit Trail (1 hour)**:

1. Write proof tests:
   - Generate valid proof, verify it passes
   - Modify proof, verify it fails
   - Modify result hash, verify proof fails
   - Modify vote set, verify proof fails
   - Missing votes, verify proof fails

2. Write inclusion tests:
   - Voter 1's vote included, verify merkle proof
   - Voter 2's vote included, verify merkle proof
   - Invalid vote ID, verify proof fails
   - Forged merkle proof, verify fails

3. End-to-end proof verification:
   - Create ballot, record votes, submit result proof, verify on-chain
   - Verify proof off-chain (reproduce locally)
   - Modify result, verify proof invalidates

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Implement vote commitment: each vote has unique ID, all votes hashed to root
- [ ] Implement result proof: SHA256(result || votes || admin_sig)
- [ ] Contract verifies result proof and stores it
- [ ] Voter can generate inclusion proof: merkle proof that vote was counted
- [ ] Contract verifies inclusion proof and confirms vote counted
- [ ] Off-chain verification: external tool can verify proof independently
- [ ] Write 20+ tests covering proof generation, verification, inclusion
- [ ] Test tampering detection: modified proof fails verification
- [ ] Test off-chain verification matches on-chain verification
- [ ] Documentation: how to generate and verify proofs off-chain

### Note for Contributors

If you're assigned to this issue, write a better description for your PR. Clearly explain what was changed, why it was needed, how it was implemented, and how it was tested.

**This is cryptography-heavy.** Proof scheme must be tamper-resistant. Test extensively with adversarial inputs: forged proofs, missing votes, modified hashes, etc. Consider external audit before production use.
title: Implement voting result verification with cryptographic commitment scheme and proof-of-inclusion

author: Just-Bamford
body:
## Description

### Problem

Current voting is direct (one person, one vote) with no delegation:

1. **No delegation**: If voter can't participate, their vote is lost
2. **No transitive voting**: Can't delegate to someone who delegates to someone else
3. **No conflict detection**: Delegate could have conflict of interest (voting on their own salary)
4. **No revocation**: Once delegated, can't change mind

This limits participation:

- Busy voter can't have expert vote for them
- Expert voter can't delegate when they don't understand an issue
- Delegates can't recuse themselves from conflicted votes

References:

- No delegation support in current contract
- `src/lib.rs` — votes recorded but no delegation tracking

### Solution

**This is a 2.5–3 hour effort:**

**Phase 1: Delegation Support (1–1.5 hours)**:

1. Implement delegation:
   - `vote_or_delegate(voter: Address, delegation_target?: Address, vote?: EncryptedVote)` — voter either votes directly or delegates
   - Store delegation: `delegations: Map<voter, delegate>`
   - Transitive resolution: if delegate → another_delegate, follow chain

2. Implement vote weight:
   - Each vote has weight (normally 1, but delegates hold multiple votes)
   - When computing tally, count votes weighted by delegation chain
   - Detect delegation cycles: delegate A → B → A (invalid)

3. Implement revocation:
   - `revoke_delegation(voter)` — voter takes back their vote
   - Must be called before voting ends
   - After revocation, voter can vote directly

**Phase 2: Conflict of Interest Detection (1–1.5 hours)**:

1. Implement conflict marking:
   - `mark_conflict(delegate: Address, ballot_id: BytesN<32>)` — delegate declares conflict
   - Can't vote or delegate on conflicted ballots
   - Delegates must explicitly mark conflicts

2. Implement conflict propagation:
   - If voter delegates to delegate with conflict, delegation invalid
   - Voter's vote goes to delegate's delegate (or discarded if chain broken)
   - Voter can choose different delegate or vote directly

3. Implement conflict audit:
   - Log all conflict declarations
   - Alert if delegate votes despite marked conflict
   - Investigate and possible revocation of delegate

**Phase 3: Tally & Verification (1 hour)**:

1. Implement delegation-aware tally:
   - Trace delegation chains: voter → delegate → final vote
   - Count votes: follow chain to final vote holder
   - Detect broken chains (delegate hasn't voted, chain stops)

2. Implement verification:
   - Proof that tally respected delegations
   - Voter can verify their vote counted (either direct or through delegate)
   - External auditor can verify all delegations were respected

3. Tests:
   - Simple delegation: voter → delegate → vote recorded with delegate
   - Transitive: voter1 → delegate1 → delegate2 → vote
   - Conflict: delegate with conflict, voter delegates to other delegate
   - Revocation: delegation revoked, voter votes directly
   - Cycles: A → B → A detected and rejected

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Implement `vote_or_delegate()` allowing direct vote or delegation
- [ ] Store delegation chain with cycle detection
- [ ] Transitive delegation: voter1 → voter2 → voter3 vote
- [ ] Vote revocation before voting ends
- [ ] Conflict marking and propagation
- [ ] Delegations invalid if delegate has conflict
- [ ] Tally traces delegation chains and counts correctly
- [ ] Verification proof that tally respected delegations
- [ ] Write 20+ tests covering delegation, transitivity, conflicts, revocation
- [ ] Test cycle detection and rejection
- [ ] Test broken chains and fallback behavior
- [ ] Documentation: delegation protocol, conflict marking, verification

### Note for Contributors

If you're assigned to this issue, write a better description for your PR. Clearly explain what was changed, why it was needed, how it was implemented, and how it was tested.

Delegation chains can create complexity — test extensively. Cycle detection is essential (infinite loops would crash). Conflict of interest is critical for fairness — test rigorously.
title: Implement liquid democracy delegation with transitive voting and conflict-of-interest detection

author: leocagli
body:
Parte de #2 (modo construcción). Depende de la capa de persistencia.

## Por qué

Editar el mundo en vivo es destructivo y va a haber accidentes. Sin poder deshacer, un error de una persona con permisos borra trabajo de horas y no hay forma de saber quién lo hizo.

## Lo que ya existe

La tabla `game_data_revisions` (`kind`, `entity_id`, `action`, `checksum`) ya registra cambios de game data. Sirve como base, pero para deshacer hace falta guardar el estado anterior, no sólo un checksum.

## Alcance

1. Log de auditoría consultable: quién cambió qué mapa, cuándo y qué cambió exactamente.
2. Deshacer la última operación sobre un mapa.
3. Rehacer.
4. Volver un mapa a una revisión anterior (rollback).
5. Diff entre dos revisiones de un mapa.

## Decisión de diseño a resolver

Guardar el estado completo del mapa por revisión es simple pero pesado: 10.000 tiles por mapa, y una sesión de edición genera muchas revisiones.

Guardar sólo el delta de cada operación es mucho más liviano y hace el undo natural, pero reconstruir un estado arbitrario obliga a reproducir la cadena.

Sugerencia: deltas, con un snapshot completo cada N revisiones para acotar el costo de reconstrucción.

## Criterios de aceptación

- [ ] Toda mutación de mapa queda en el log con autor, fecha y contenido del cambio
- [ ] Deshacer revierte exactamente la última operación
- [ ] Rehacer restaura lo deshecho
- [ ] Se puede volver a una revisión anterior arbitraria
- [ ] El diff entre dos revisiones es legible
- [ ] Deshacer una operación ya publicada exige republicar (no cambia el mundo en silencio)
- [ ] Tests de integración

## Archivos relevantes

- `api/src/repositories/` (todos los repos que ya escriben en `game_data_revisions`)
- `api/schema.sql`
title: Etapa 3: log de auditoria, deshacer y rollback de mapas
