body:
**Area:** `src/App.tsx`

**Description**
`App.tsx`'s `<Routes>` (lines 46–58) only defines: `/`, `/analytics`, `/admin`,
`/dev/components`, `/activity`, and `/campaigns/:id`. It does not route:
`CampaignsPage` (Issue 4), `CreateCampaignPage` (exists and is fully wired to real
`useCreateCampaign`/`useRegisterCampaign` hooks per `pages/CreateCampaignPage.tsx`, but is
unreachable), the real `InvestorDashboardPage` (see Issue 6), `FarmerDashboardPage`, or
`ProfilePage` (both placeholders exported from `pages/index.tsx`). There is also no
wildcard `*` route rendering `NotFoundPage`, even though that component exists
specifically for this purpose.

**Problem**
Several genuinely-built, tested features — campaign creation being the most significant,
since it's fully wired to real contract calls — are completely unreachable through the
running application. A user hitting an unrecognized URL gets a blank page (no route
matches, so `<Routes>` renders nothing) instead of the `NotFoundPage` the app already has
for that case. This was also flagged as a known gap in
`docs/accessibility-audit.md` ("aren't wired into `App.tsx`'s router yet — a pre-existing
gap, not introduced by this PR").

**Suggested Implementation**
- Add routes for `/campaigns` (Issue 4's list page), `/campaigns/new` (`CreateCampaignPage`),
  `/investor` (the real `InvestorDashboardPage`, after resolving Issue 6), `/farmer`
  (`FarmerDashboardPage`, once it's a real implementation rather than a placeholder), and
  `/profile` (`ProfilePage`).
- Add a final `<Route path="*" element={<NotFoundPage />} />`.
- Add nav links for the newly-reachable routes in `AppLayout`'s header/nav, consistent with
  the existing `/activity` link.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] Every page component under `src/pages/` is reachable via a route (or is explicitly
      documented as intentionally unrouted, e.g. `Playground`/dev-only pages).
- [ ] Visiting an unknown path renders `NotFoundPage`.
- [ ] Primary nav includes working links to the newly-routed pages.
title: Most built pages are never wired into the router, and there is no catch-all 404 route

author: grantfox-oss
body:
**Area:** `src/pages/index.tsx` (lines 77–85), `src/pages/InvestorDashboardPage.tsx`

**Description**
`pages/index.tsx` defines and exports its own `InvestorDashboardPage` placeholder
component (a static `PlaceholderPage`). A separate, fully-built, feature-complete
component also named `InvestorDashboardPage` exists in `pages/InvestorDashboardPage.tsx`
(the one covered in Issue 3). Both are named exports with the same identifier, from two
different modules, and neither is currently imported by `App.tsx`.

**Problem**
This is a correctness/maintainability landmine: `import { InvestorDashboardPage } from './pages'`
silently gets the placeholder, while `import { InvestorDashboardPage } from './pages/InvestorDashboardPage'`
gets the real one — there's nothing to stop a future contributor (e.g. whoever resolves
Issue 5's routing gap) from wiring up the wrong one and shipping a placeholder where the
real dashboard was intended, with no compiler error to catch it.

**Suggested Implementation**
- Remove the placeholder `InvestorDashboardPage` from `pages/index.tsx` entirely (and its
  `PlaceholderPage` usage), since a real implementation already exists.
- Have `pages/index.tsx` re-export the real one instead, the same way it already does for
  `CampaignDetailPage`, `CreateCampaignPage`, `AdminDashboardPage`, and `ActivityFeedPage`
  (see the comment on line 87: `// ActivityFeedPage is the real implementation exported
  from ./ActivityFeedPage` — the same pattern should apply here).
- Audit `FarmerDashboardPage` and `ProfilePage` in `pages/index.tsx` for the same risk once
  real implementations for those are built.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] Only one component/export named `InvestorDashboardPage` exists in the codebase.
- [ ] `pages/index.tsx` re-exports the real implementation, matching the pattern already
      used for the other real pages.
- [ ] No import path can resolve to a placeholder when a real page exists for that route.
title: Two different components are both named/exported as `InvestorDashboardPage`

author: grantfox-oss
body:
**Area:** `src/hooks/useAdminCampaigns.ts`, `src/hooks/useCampaignAnalytics.ts`,
`src/lib/soroban/events.ts`

**Description**
`useAdminCampaigns()` discovers campaigns by scanning `ProductionEscrowContract` events
from `startLedger` (current ledger minus `LOOKBACK_LEDGERS`, default `120_000` ledgers,
`useAdminCampaigns.ts` lines 12–19) forward, since there is no on-chain "list all
campaigns" getter (correctly noted in the code comment on lines 36–40).
`useCampaignAnalytics.ts` uses the same bounded-lookback approach. `lib/soroban/events.ts`
additionally hard-caps at `MAX_PAGES = 50` pages of 100 events each per load.

**Problem**
Any campaign created before the lookback window (roughly the last ~120,000 ledgers, and
further limited by however much event history the configured Soroban RPC provider actually
retains — public RPC providers commonly retain far less than a full ledger's worth of
history) becomes permanently invisible to the Admin Dashboard and Analytics Dashboard, with
no error, warning, or way to page further back. As the chain accumulates history, this
dashboard will silently show fewer and fewer of the platform's real campaigns over time,
which is especially problematic for the Admin Dashboard — an admin could believe there are
no actionable campaigns when in fact there are, just outside the scan window.

**Suggested Implementation**
- Make the lookback window and RPC retention limits visible in the UI (e.g. "Showing
  campaigns created in the last N days; older campaigns may not appear") rather than
  failing silently.
- Prefer a backend-indexed source of truth once available (`lib/api/` already has typed
  client scaffolding — see Issue 3's note that it's currently unused by any page) instead
  of relying solely on client-side RPC event scanning, which doesn't scale with chain
  history.
- If RPC event scanning remains the primary/fallback mechanism, consider a registry-based
  campaign counter/index (see the contracts-side registry work) as a way to enumerate all
  known campaign ids directly, rather than reconstructing the set from a bounded event
  window.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] The Admin and Analytics dashboards clearly indicate when campaign discovery is
      limited by a lookback/history window, rather than presenting a partial list as if it
      were complete.
- [ ] A documented, tested strategy exists for surfacing campaigns older than the lookback
      window (backend index, on-chain counter, or explicit "load older" pagination).
- [ ] Behavior is covered by a test simulating a campaign event outside the current lookback
      window.
title: Admin/Analytics campaign discovery silently drops campaigns older than the event lookback window

author: grantfox-oss
body:
**Area:** `src/components/campaign/FundCampaignModal.tsx`, `src/pages/CampaignDetailPage.tsx`,
`src/pages/InvestorDashboardPage.tsx`, `src/components/investor/InvestmentCard.tsx`,
`src/components/investor/InvestorSummaryStats.tsx`

**Description**
The rest of the app uses a shared earth-tone design system (`soil`/`leaf`/`status-*`
Tailwind tokens defined in `tailwind.config.ts`, used by `Header`, `StatTile`, `ChartCard`,
`LifecycleStepper`, `CreateCampaignPage`, etc.). The five files listed above instead use raw
Tailwind default colors (`slate`, `emerald`, `amber`) with hardcoded hex-adjacent utility
classes, forming a second, independent, inconsistent design system. This is already
explicitly called out as a known, unresolved issue in `docs/accessibility-audit.md`
("this is exactly the 'independently-built pages regress accessibility' failure mode issue
#65 describes... Fully unifying the two design systems is a larger change than an a11y/
contrast fix and is called out as a follow-up below rather than attempted here.").

**Problem**
Beyond the visual inconsistency, this doubles the maintenance burden for anything
appearance-related (the accessibility audit had to separately verify and fix contrast for
both palettes) and makes it easy for future changes to one system to silently miss the
other, exactly as already happened once. It also affects some of the very pages this audit
identifies as needing rework (Issues 1–3), so unifying the design system is a natural
companion to fixing their data-wiring.

**Suggested Implementation**
- Migrate the five listed files from `slate`/`emerald`/`amber` utility classes to the
  shared `soil`/`leaf`/`status-*` tokens and existing shared components (`Button`, `Card`,
  `Badge`/`StatusBadge`, `Modal`) already used elsewhere in the app.
  `FundCampaignModal` already migrated to the shared `<Modal>` component for its dialog
  chrome (per the accessibility audit) — extend the same consolidation to color tokens and
  remaining bespoke markup (e.g. hand-rolled buttons instead of the shared `Button`
  component).
- Do this migration alongside Issues 1–3's data-wiring fixes where practical, since those
  files are being substantially rewritten anyway.
- Re-run the `jest-axe`/contrast checks from `src/__tests__/accessibility.test.tsx` after
  migration to confirm no regression.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] The five listed files use the shared `soil`/`leaf`/`status-*` design tokens and
      shared UI components instead of a separate ad hoc palette.
- [ ] No new color-contrast regressions, verified by the existing accessibility test suite.
- [ ] `docs/accessibility-audit.md`'s "two design systems" follow-up note can be closed out.
title: Two incompatible design systems are mixed across the app

author: grantfox-oss
body:
**Area:** `registry/src/types.rs` (`DataKey::FarmerCount`, `DataKey::CampaignCount`),
`registry/src/farmer.rs`, `registry/src/campaign.rs`

**Description**
`registry/src/types.rs` declares `DataKey::FarmerCount` and `DataKey::CampaignCount`
(lines 82–83), but neither is ever read or written anywhere in the crate — confirmed by
grep, they appear only in the enum definition. There is no `get_all_campaigns`,
`get_all_farmers`, or any counter-based enumeration. The only listing capability that
exists is `get_campaigns_by_farmer` (per-farmer), added alongside `CampaignRecord`.

**Problem**
There is no way for any off-chain consumer to ask "what campaigns exist?" without already
knowing every campaign id in advance. This is a real, load-bearing gap: the client's admin
and analytics dashboards work around it by scanning `ProductionEscrowContract`'s recent
event history within a bounded lookback window (see `client/src/hooks/useAdminCampaigns.ts`),
which is unreliable — campaigns created before the lookback window (or before whatever
history the configured RPC provider retains) silently disappear from those views. A
proper on-chain enumeration primitive in the registry — which already exists specifically
to be "the source of truth... supports discovery and indexing" per the top-level
`README.md` — would remove the need for that fragile workaround entirely.

**Suggested Implementation**
- Increment `CampaignCount` in `register_campaign` (and/or `link_campaign_escrow`) and
  `FarmerCount` in `register_farmer`, and expose `get_campaign_count`/`get_farmer_count`
  getters.
- Add a way to enumerate by index — e.g. store a `DataKey::CampaignIndex(u64)` mapping a
  sequential index to a campaign id (populated alongside the count), so a client can page
  through `0..campaign_count` — or, cheaper, expose a `get_campaign_ids(offset, limit)`
  paginated getter backed by an append-only `Vec<u64>`, being mindful of the same
  unbounded-growth concern raised in Issue 9 below.
- Add tests covering count accuracy after multiple registrations and pagination
  correctness.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] A client can retrieve the full set of registered campaign ids (paginated) without
      relying on event-log scanning.
- [ ] `CampaignCount`/`FarmerCount` (or their replacement) are actually populated and
      accurate.
- [ ] `INTEGRATION.md` documents the new discovery method as the recommended path over
      event scanning.
title: [Contract] No on-chain way to enumerate all registered campaigns or farmers

author: grantfox-oss
body:
**Area:** `registry/src/campaign.rs`

**Description**
`register_campaign` (lines 5–30) creates a `CampaignInfo { id, farmer, title, description, created_at }`.
`link_campaign_escrow` (lines 39–72) separately creates a `CampaignRecord { campaign_id, farmer, escrow_contract, crop_metadata, region_metadata, status }`
for what is, by id convention, meant to be the same logical campaign. `link_campaign_escrow`
only checks `storage::has_campaign_record(env, campaign_id)` (i.e. whether it's already
been linked) — it never checks `storage::has_campaign(env, campaign_id)` (whether that id
was ever registered via `register_campaign` in the first place), and it takes its own
independent `farmer: &Address` parameter rather than reading it from the existing
`CampaignInfo`.

**Problem**
Concretely, today it's possible to:
- Call `link_campaign_escrow` for a `campaign_id` that was never `register_campaign`'d,
  producing a `CampaignRecord` with no corresponding title/description anywhere.
- Call `register_campaign` and `link_campaign_escrow` for the same `campaign_id` with two
  *different* `farmer` addresses, since nothing cross-checks them — leaving the registry
  with two disagreeing opinions about who owns the campaign.

**Suggested Implementation**
- Have `link_campaign_escrow` require `storage::has_campaign(env, campaign_id)` (i.e.
  `register_campaign` must happen first) and read `farmer` from the existing `CampaignInfo`
  rather than accepting it as a separate, independently-trusted parameter — or, if a
  farmer parameter must remain for the approved-contract call path, assert it matches the
  registered `CampaignInfo.farmer` and panic on mismatch.
- Add tests for: linking before registering (should fail), and linking with a mismatched
  farmer address (should fail).

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] `link_campaign_escrow` cannot succeed for a campaign id that hasn't been
      `register_campaign`'d.
- [ ] `CampaignInfo.farmer` and `CampaignRecord.farmer` cannot disagree for the same
      campaign id.
- [ ] Both new failure cases are covered by tests.
title: [Contract] `register_campaign` and `link_campaign_escrow` are independent, unvalidated, and can produce inconsistent records for the same campaign id

author: grantfox-oss
body:
**Area:** `production_escrow/src/storage.rs`, `registry/src/storage.rs`

**Description**
Every write path in both contracts calls `extend_persistent_ttl`/`extend_instance_ttl`
after mutating storage — but once a campaign reaches a terminal state (`Settled`,
`Failed`, `Resolved` on the escrow side), nothing ever touches its `Campaign`, `Dispute`,
`Tranches`, or `HarvestRecord` entries again. Soroban persistent entries whose TTL lapses
become archived and unreadable until explicitly restored (`RestoreFootprintOp`); nothing
in this codebase performs or documents that restore step.

**Problem**
A campaign that settles today and is queried again after its persistent entries' TTL
expires (whenever that is, per the `PERSISTENT_LIFETIME_THRESHOLD`/`PERSISTENT_BUMP_AMOUNT`
constants — 30/90 days' worth of ledgers in both contracts) will fail to read: `get_campaign`
and friends `.unwrap()` directly on the storage read (see Issue 8 in this file), so an
archived entry doesn't degrade gracefully — it panics. For a platform whose whole point is
an auditable campaign history, permanently losing read access to completed campaigns after
a few months unless someone proactively restores them is a significant, easy-to-miss
operational risk.

**Suggested Implementation**
- Document this explicitly in both contracts' READMEs: which entries stop being touched
  once terminal, what the resulting TTL/archival timeline is, and that a periodic
  `RestoreFootprintOp` (or an on-chain "touch" method some off-chain job calls
  periodically) is required to keep historical campaigns readable indefinitely.
- Consider adding a permissionless `touch_campaign(campaign_id)` method that just extends
  TTL without changing any other state, so an indexer/keeper job can cheaply keep
  important historical campaigns alive without needing a full restore operation.
- At minimum, wrap the getters' storage reads for terminal-state entries with a clearer
  panic message pointing at this operational requirement, until Issue 8 (below) is
  addressed more generally.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] The TTL/archival behavior for terminal campaigns is documented in both contract
      READMEs.
- [ ] Either a `touch`-style keep-alive method exists, or the operational requirement to
      run `RestoreFootprintOp` periodically is documented with enough detail (which keys,
      what cadence) for an indexer/ops team to act on it.
title: [Contract] Terminal campaigns' storage entries stop being TTL-extended and can be archived, making settled history unreadable

author: grantfox-oss
body:
**Area:** `registry/src/farmer.rs`, `registry/src/campaign.rs`

**Description**
`register_farmer` (`farmer.rs` lines 5–29) and `register_campaign` (`campaign.rs` lines
5–30) both `panic!` unconditionally on any second call for the same farmer address or
campaign id (`"farmer already registered"` / `"campaign already registered"`). Neither
module has an `update_farmer_profile` or `update_campaign_metadata` function.

**Problem**
A farmer who makes a typo in their name/location, relocates, or a campaign whose
title/description needs correcting before funding starts has no on-chain way to fix it —
these are permanently write-once fields.

**Suggested Implementation**
- Add `update_farmer_profile(env, farmer, name, location)` requiring
  `farmer.require_auth()` and that the farmer is already registered.
- Add `update_campaign_metadata(env, campaign_id, farmer, title, description)` requiring
  the caller to be the campaign's registered farmer, and — coordinating with Issue 1's
  status mirroring — reasonably restricted to before the campaign has left `Active`/`Funding`
  status, if that mirrored status is available at call time.
- Emit distinct update events so indexers can tell "created" from "updated".
- Add tests for successful updates, unauthorized attempts, and updates to nonexistent
  records.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] A farmer can update their own profile; no one else can update it for them.
- [ ] A campaign's registered farmer can update its title/description; no one else can.
- [ ] Updating a nonexistent farmer/campaign fails with a clear, documented error.
- [ ] New events are added to `INTEGRATION.md`'s event tables and covered by
      `verify_documented_events.rs`.
title: [Contract] No update path for a farmer's profile or a campaign's registered title/description

body:
- Description: The app defaults to `file:./dev.db` when `DATABASE_URL` is unset.
- Problem: In production this fallback could silently start with an embedded DB, causing data loss and operational confusion.

author: grantfox-oss
body:
**Area:** `server/src/indexer/parsers/event-parser.service.ts` (`persistEvent`, lines
831–916, and the `handle*` methods it dispatches to)

**Description**
`persistEvent()` dispatches to a handler (e.g. `handleCampaignInvested`, lines 949–977)
that performs multiple, separate `await this.prisma.*` calls — none wrapped in
`prisma.$transaction(...)` (confirmed: `$transaction` is not used anywhere in `server/src`).
Only after the handler returns does `persistEvent` write the idempotency-marking
`Transaction` row (lines 899–913), which is also what the top-level idempotency check at
the top of `persistEvent` (`existing = await this.prisma.transaction.findUnique(...)`,
lines 832–835) relies on to skip already-processed events.

**Problem**
Take `handleCampaignInvested`: it calls `prisma.investment.create(...)` and then
`prisma.campaign.update(...)`. If the second call throws for any reason (the campaign row
not existing yet, a transient DB error, a constraint violation) *after* the first
succeeded, the `Investment` row is now permanently created but `Campaign.totalFunded` was
never incremented — and because the error propagates up and is caught by
`processEvent`'s outer `try/catch` (`event-parser.service.ts` lines 85–109, which logs and
swallows), execution never reaches the `Transaction` row write that marks this event as
processed. On the *next* poll, this event is not in the in-memory
`processedEventIds` (per `SorobanEventListenerService`, that Set is only populated once
per process lifetime and isn't consulted for correctness — the real idempotency guard is
the `Transaction` row lookup), so it gets reprocessed — and `prisma.investment.create`
immediately fails again with a unique-constraint violation on the same `id` (the event id),
since that row already exists from the first partial attempt. This event can now *never*
successfully complete: every future poll retries it, fails at the same step, and it never
gets marked processed — a permanent poison pill that also spams error logs forever.

**Suggested Implementation**
- Wrap each `handle*` method's writes, plus the final `Transaction` row insert in
  `persistEvent`, in a single `prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => { ... })` so a partial
  failure rolls back cleanly and the event is retried from a consistent state next poll.
- Since the handlers currently take `this.prisma` implicitly via `this.prisma.*` calls,
  this will require threading a transaction client (`tx`) through each `handle*` method
  instead of the module-level `this.prisma` — a real refactor across every handler, not a
  one-line fix.
- Add a test that forces the second write in a two-write handler to fail and asserts
  *nothing* was persisted (no orphaned `Investment` row) and the event is retried
  successfully on the next call once the fault is removed.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] Every event handler's writes (plus the idempotency-marking `Transaction` row) commit
      or roll back atomically.
- [ ] A simulated mid-handler failure leaves zero partial rows, verified by a test.
- [ ] The same event, retried after a transient failure, succeeds and is marked processed
      exactly once — no permanent poison-pill state is reachable.
title: [Backend] Event handlers aren't wrapped in a database transaction, so a partial failure creates a permanently un-retryable "poison pill" event

author: grantfox-oss
body:
**Area:** `server/src/database/database.module.ts` (line 11) vs.
`server/src/config/configuration.ts` (line 48) / `env.validation.ts` (line 15)

**Description**
`configuration.ts` and `env.validation.ts` both define `DATABASE_URL`'s default as
`'file:./dev.db'`, consumed through the typed, validated `ConfigService`. But
`DatabaseModule`'s Prisma client factory does its own, completely separate resolution:

```ts
const url = process.env.DATABASE_URL || 'file:./dev.db';
```

reading `process.env` directly rather than injecting `ConfigService`.

**Problem**
This is a real architectural inconsistency with a concrete consequence: any future fix to
`DATABASE_URL` validation (e.g. requiring it in production, per the reasonable instinct
that a service should fail fast rather than silently start against a local SQLite file) —
if applied only to `env.validation.ts`/`configuration.ts` — would **not** actually stop
`DatabaseModule` from connecting to `file:./dev.db` in production, since it never consults
that validated config at all. The two code paths can silently diverge from each other with
no error, since Joi validation on `envValidationSchema` doesn't gate what
`DatabaseModule`'s factory independently reads.

**Suggested Implementation**
- Change `DatabaseModule`'s `PrismaClient` factory to inject `ConfigService` and read
  `config.get<string>('db.url')`, matching how every other config value is consumed in the
  app, removing the raw `process.env` read entirely.
- Once unified, add production-mode validation (e.g. a custom Joi rule or a bootstrap
  check) that rejects a `file:`-scheme `DATABASE_URL` when `NODE_ENV=production`, and
  verify — with a test — that this actually prevents `DatabaseModule` from constructing a
  client against a local file in that mode (closing the gap this issue is really about,
  not just moving the duplicate default around).

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] `DatabaseModule` resolves `DATABASE_URL` exclusively through `ConfigService`, with no
      direct `process.env` read remaining.
- [ ] A production-mode guard against the local-file default exists and is proven, by
      test, to actually affect the Prisma client `DatabaseModule` constructs — not just
      the value `ConfigService.get('db.url')` returns.
title: [Backend] `DATABASE_URL` resolution is duplicated and inconsistent — fixing the validated config path wouldn't change what database the app actually uses

author: grantfox-oss
body:
**Area:** `server/src/config/configuration.ts` (line 62), `env.validation.ts` (line 25)

**Description**
`EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS` is defined, validated (`Joi.number().min(1).max(7).default(7)`),
and exposed via `SorobanConfig.eventRetentionDays` — but a full search of `server/src`
turns up no scheduled job, no `@nestjs/schedule` dependency (it's not in `package.json`),
and no code anywhere that reads `soroban.eventRetentionDays` outside its own definition.

**Problem**
This is a fully-specified, documented config knob for a feature that was never built: the
`Transaction` table (the append-only audit log every indexed event writes a row into, per
`persistEvent`) has no cleanup path at all and will grow unbounded indefinitely, regardless
of what an operator sets `EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS` to. An operator reading the `.env.example`/
config schema would reasonably assume old data is being pruned; it isn't.

**Suggested Implementation**
- Add `@nestjs/schedule`, and a scheduled job (e.g. daily) that deletes `Transaction` rows
  older than `soroban.eventRetentionDays`, batched to avoid a single huge delete on a large
  table.
- Decide and document whether retention applies only to the generic `Transaction` audit
  log or also to domain rows (`Investment`, `Tranche`, `Dispute`) — deleting those would
  lose real financial history, so the safer default is almost certainly "audit log only."
- Log/emit a metric for each cleanup run (rows deleted, duration) so it's observable.
- Add a test verifying rows older than the retention window are deleted and rows within it
  are preserved.

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] A scheduled cleanup job exists, runs on the configured cadence, and respects
      `EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS`.
- [ ] The job is scoped to audit-only data unless a deliberate decision is documented to
      include domain rows.
- [ ] Covered by a test exercising both the "older than retention" and "within retention"
      cases.
title: [Backend] `EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS` is fully validated as a config option but no retention or cleanup job exists anywhere

visible as more of `CampaignDetailPage` gets wired to real functionality

  more consistently-used one across `CampaignAdminPanel`, `StatusBadge`,
  `LifecycleStepper`) and migrate `CampaignDetailPage.tsx`,
  `FundCampaignModal.tsx`, and `InvestorDashboardPage.tsx` to it.

- `client/src/components/campaign/FundCampaignModal.tsx`

author: RUKAYAT-CODER
body:
### Background
There is no referral/invitation mechanism, so users cannot invite others and earn rewards for growth they drive. A referral program needs: unique per-user referral codes, signup attribution, a qualification rule (the referred user must reach a qualifying milestone — e.g. their first approved submission — before a reward is credited), anti-abuse checks (self-referral, duplicate/circular attribution), and a reward ledger. This issue covers the **backend API and logic only** (the referral UI is tracked separately).

### Implementation Plan

**Codes, attribution, and API**
- New `referrals` module. `ReferralsService` generates a stable, unique referral code per user, resolves a code to its owner, and records an attribution when a new user signs up with a code.
- `ReferralsController` exposes: get my referral code/link, list my referrals and their status, and view credited rewards (auth-guarded).
- Capture the referral code during signup in `AuthService` and create a pending attribution linked to the new user; reject self-referral and codes that would form a circular attribution.

**Qualification and reward crediting**
- Persist a `Referral` entity (referrer, referred user, code, status: pending/qualified/rewarded/rejected, timestamps) and a `ReferralReward` ledger entity, plus a migration.
- Add a qualifying-event hook in `SubmissionsService` (e.g. first approved submission by the referred user) that enqueues reward processing.
- A `referral-reward` BullMQ processor performs anti-abuse validation and credits the reward idempotently, moving the referral to `rewarded`; it dead-letters/records rejected referrals.

**Wiring**
- Register the queue/processor in the jobs module and `ReferralsModule` in `app.module.ts`.

### Affected Files (10–11)
- `BackEnd/src/modules/referrals/referrals.module.ts` (new)
- `BackEnd/src/modules/referrals/referrals.service.ts` (new)
- `BackEnd/src/modules/referrals/referrals.controller.ts` (new)
- `BackEnd/src/modules/referrals/entities/referral.entity.ts` (new)
- `BackEnd/src/modules/referrals/entities/referral-reward.entity.ts` (new)
- `BackEnd/src/database/migrations/<ts>-add-referrals.ts` (new)
- `BackEnd/src/modules/jobs/processors/referral-reward.processor.ts` (new)
- `BackEnd/src/modules/auth/auth.service.ts`
- `BackEnd/src/modules/submissions/submissions.service.ts`
- `BackEnd/src/modules/jobs/jobs.module.ts`
- `BackEnd/src/app.module.ts`

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each user has a unique referral code; signing up with a code creates a pending attribution
- [ ] Self-referral and circular/duplicate attributions are rejected
- [ ] A referral becomes `qualified` on the referred user's qualifying milestone and is then rewarded exactly once (idempotent crediting)
- [ ] Referral status and reward ledger are queryable via the API
- [ ] Unit + integration tests cover attribution, anti-abuse rejection, qualification, and idempotent reward crediting
- [ ] No regression in signup/submission flows; backend CI passes
- [ ] Program rules and API documented; module CHANGELOG updated
title: Add a backend referral & invitation program with qualification-based reward attribution

author: akintewe
body:
This app now has several independent flows that each move real ECHO/XLM across two systems with fundamentally different consistency models: Stellar (an external, eventually-consistent ledger this app doesn't control) and Supabase (this app's own, immediately-consistent internal database). `send-echo` (gifts), `settle-leaderboard-rewards` (weekly payouts), the streak-freeze purchase flow (`streak_freezes` insert with a 5 ECHO cost), and wallet creation/funding each independently implement "do the Stellar operation, then write the internal record" as two separate steps with no shared framework ensuring both happen or neither does. The already-filed `settle-leaderboard-rewards` reliability issue found exactly this failure mode in one specific place (a Stellar payment succeeding while the `echo_rewards` insert silently fails) — but that's one symptom of a pattern repeated, with different specific bugs, everywhere this app touches both systems in the same operation.

This issue is about building the actual general solution, not patching each flow's specific instance of the same underlying architectural gap one at a time.

Scope:
- Design a saga/compensating-transaction framework for every flow that spans Stellar + Supabase: each such operation gets modeled as an explicit sequence of steps with a defined compensating action for each step that can fail after a prior step succeeded (e.g. "Stellar payment succeeded, ledger write failed" → the compensating action isn't necessarily "reverse the Stellar payment" — Stellar transactions are irreversible — but must be "reliably retry the ledger write until it succeeds, with the operation held in a recoverable pending state in the meantime, never silently reported as failed or dropped")
- Build a durable operation log (a table tracking in-flight and completed multi-step operations, their current step, and outcome) so a crashed or restarted process can resume or reconcile an interrupted operation instead of losing track of it entirely — this is the actual hard infrastructure piece the framework needs underneath it
- Migrate `send-echo`, `settle-leaderboard-rewards`, and the streak-freeze purchase flow onto this framework, replacing each one's current ad hoc "do both steps and hope" approach
- Build a reconciliation job (scheduled, `pg_cron`-driven like the other scheduled jobs in this codebase) that periodically compares recent Stellar transaction history for this app's accounts against internal ledger records and flags — or where safe, auto-heals — any divergence, as a second line of defense beyond the saga framework itself catching failures at operation time
- This is explicitly a hard, foundational piece of infrastructure — expect it to take real design iteration, and expect the existing `settle-leaderboard-rewards` reliability issue to become effectively superseded/absorbed by this one once it lands, rather than needing its own narrower fix on top of a framework that already solves the general problem

Acceptance criteria:
- Every ECHO/XLM-moving flow in this app uses the shared saga framework, with no flow able to reach a state where a Stellar operation succeeded but the corresponding internal record is silently missing or inconsistent
- A deliberately interrupted operation (kill the process mid-flow in a test) is either resumed to completion or clearly surfaced as needing reconciliation — never silently lost
- The scheduled reconciliation job catches a manually introduced discrepancy between on-chain and internal ledger state within one run cycle
title: feat(stellar): build a saga/compensating-transaction framework for every flow that spans Stellar and Supabase

author: akintewe
body:
`MoodSyncService` queues mood entries created offline and syncs them on reconnect — creation only, single entity type, with (per the already-filed conflict-resolution issue) no real handling for edits that diverge from server state. Habit logging (per the already-filed offline-support gap) has no offline handling at all. Gifts, social posts, follows, and everything else in this app are online-only by default. Each of these is a separate, entity-specific piece of ad hoc offline plumbing, or missing entirely — there's no general local-first architecture underneath any of it.

This issue is the full architectural version of that problem: a genuine local-first data layer covering every entity type this app has, with principled conflict resolution rather than per-entity bespoke queues bolted on one at a time as each gap gets separately noticed and separately patched.

Scope:
- Design and implement a local-first storage layer (on top of, or replacing, `offline_storage_service.dart`'s current scope) that every mutable entity type in this app writes through — mood entries, habit logs, gifts, social posts/stories, follows — rather than each feature independently deciding whether and how to support offline use
- Use a principled conflict-resolution mechanism designed once, generically, rather than per-entity ad hoc rules: a version-vector or hybrid-logical-clock scheme is a reasonable fit here (full CRDTs are likely overkill for this app's actual data shapes — mostly simple records without deep nested concurrent-editable structure — but evaluate against the app's real entity shapes rather than assuming either extreme without checking)
- Every entity needs a defined merge/resolution policy appropriate to its own semantics — a mood entry's `notes` field probably wants last-write-wins-with-conflict-surfaced (per the already-filed mood-specific issue), while something like "did I complete this habit today" is closer to a boolean toggle where the resolution rule can be simpler and more automatic; don't apply one blanket policy to every entity type without considering whether it actually fits
- Build a genuinely reliable background sync trigger — connectivity-restored is necessary but not sufficient (a connection can flap, or come back with limited/metered bandwidth where the app should be smarter about sync ordering/prioritization) — consider `WorkManager`/`BGTaskScheduler`-backed background sync so queued writes eventually flush even if the user doesn't happen to reopen the app right when connectivity returns
- This absorbs and generalizes the already-filed habit-offline-support and mood-edit-conflict issues rather than needing them solved narrowly and separately first — but if those land first as incremental steps before this larger effort starts, that's fine; this issue is about the durable general architecture, not about blocking on sequencing
- Tests: entity-type-agnostic conflict scenarios (concurrent edits across two simulated devices for several different entity types) each resolve according to their entity-appropriate policy, and a flaky/metered connectivity simulation still eventually converges to full sync

Acceptance criteria:
- Every mutable entity type in the app is safely usable offline, with entity-appropriate conflict resolution, through one shared local-first architecture rather than N separate bespoke implementations
- A simulated flaky-connectivity scenario across multiple entity types and multiple "devices" eventually converges to consistent state with no silently lost writes
title: feat(sync): build a general local-first architecture with principled conflict resolution across every entity type

author: akintewe
body:
`generate-insight` currently reads a user's raw mood/habit/notes data server-side to produce AI predictions and suggestions via Gemini. The already-filed field-level encryption issue for mood notes explicitly flags this as the hard part of that work: encrypting notes client-side breaks server-side insight generation unless something else takes its place, and punts on a real answer beyond a coarse per-entry opt-out. This issue is that real answer: a genuinely privacy-preserving insight pipeline that produces the same kind of personalized, pattern-aware output the current system does, without the server ever seeing plaintext reflection content.

Scope:
- Move embedding generation on-device: run a small, on-device embedding model (a compact sentence-embedding model small enough to ship in a mobile app — evaluate real options against actual size/latency/battery budgets rather than assuming any specific model works without checking) over each entry's plaintext locally, before it's ever encrypted and sent to the server. The embedding vector, not the raw text, is what leaves the device
- Maintain a per-user local index of historical entry embeddings (on-device vector storage — doesn't need to be a full vector database given per-user data volumes here are small; a straightforward in-memory or lightweight on-disk index is proportionate) enabling on-device similarity search: "which past entries resemble this one" computed locally, never requiring the server to see the content being compared
- Redesign insight generation around what's now possible without server-side plaintext access: either the LLM call itself moves on-device (a much bigger ask, likely out of scope for a first version given mobile LLM inference constraints — note this explicitly rather than silently attempting it) or the server receives only embeddings/derived numerical features (mood score trends, embedding-similarity clusters, habit-completion patterns) sufficient to generate meaningful predictions/suggestions without ever reconstructing the actual text content — decide and clearly document which approach this issue actually implements, since claiming "AI insights with zero server-side content access" needs to be true of whatever's actually shipped, not aspirational
- This needs to produce insight quality genuinely comparable to today's system to be worth shipping — benchmark generated insights (prediction relevance, suggestion usefulness) against the current plaintext-based pipeline on a real or representative dataset before considering this complete, not just "it runs and returns something"
- Coordinate explicitly with the field-level encryption issue this depends on/complements — this issue's on-device embedding step is what makes it possible for that issue's "notes are encrypted, AI still works" requirement to be genuinely true rather than solved by a workaround that quietly reduces how many entries get real insight coverage

Acceptance criteria:
- Insight generation runs without the server ever receiving decryptable plaintext note content, verified by inspecting exactly what data crosses the network during a real insight-generation request
- Insight quality (measured against a defined rubric or comparison set) is genuinely comparable to the current server-side-plaintext pipeline, not a degraded fallback
title: feat(ai): build an on-device, privacy-preserving embedding pipeline so AI insights work without server-side plaintext access

author: cybermax4200
body:
### Why this matters now
The notification system is v0.2-complete and directly tied to streak reminders, reward confirmations, and the `prefsStore` rehydration bug (Issue 8). `NotificationPreferencesScreen` is the only user-facing control for notification preferences, but it has no tests at all. Any regression in toggle persistence, quiet-hours validation, or the `allEnabled` master switch is invisible in CI.

### Problem / What
`src/screens/NotificationPreferencesScreen.tsx` (243 lines) contains:
- A master enable/disable toggle backed by `prefsStore.setAllEnabled`
- Per-type toggles for each `NOTIFICATION_TYPES` value backed by `prefsStore.toggleType`
- Quiet-hours from/to time pickers backed by `prefsStore.setQuietHours`
- Inline validation (from < to, valid HH:MM format)

None of these interactions have a test file. The nearest coverage is `prefsStore.test.ts` (which tests only the store, not the screen).

### Key Challenges
- The screen imports `@notifee/react-native` indirectly via `prefsStore.toggleType` (which cancels notifications asynchronously). The mock in `__mocks__` or `rn-modules.ts` must be extended.
- Quiet-hours validation involves parsing time strings; edge cases (midnight wrap `22:00–07:00`, identical from/to) must be tested.
- The component uses `TouchableOpacity` switches rather than platform `Switch` — `fireEvent.press` is the right interaction method.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test file `src/__tests__/NotificationPreferencesScreen.test.tsx` created.
- [ ] Tests cover: master toggle enables/disables all notifications, per-type toggle persists to store, quiet-hours update validates and persists, invalid time input shows an error.
- [ ] All tests pass in CI with `npm test`.

### Relevant files / functions
- `src/screens/NotificationPreferencesScreen.tsx`
- `src/store/prefsStore.ts`
- `src/__tests__/__mocks__/rn-modules.ts` — add notifee mock if absent

### Out of scope
- Integration testing with the actual notification delivery system.
- Testing `scheduleDailyStreakReminder` (separate concern).
title: `[Testing] Zero test coverage for NotificationPreferencesScreen — toggle, quiet-hours, and all-disable paths`
